category_title: Students with reactive study habits and entity-based beliefs about academic ability
minimal_context: During a peer fellow study session, the tutor asks the student to reflect on their recent Biology exam results to determine the causes of their academic difficulty.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's take some time in our peer fellow session today to reflect on the recent Biology exam results and determine the causes of any difficulties you might have had.

STUDENT: I got my grade back and it's really disappointing. I studied the night before the exam and took breaks while studying, but I guess I can't do this. I'm not a Biology person.

TUTOR: What other study habits did you use to prepare for the exam?

STUDENT: I usually study alone primarily. But really, the professor talks too fast. The test didn't cover the lectures in class.

TUTOR: How do you plan to prepare for the next exam?

STUDENT: She doesn't teach, care, or want us to pass, so I'm not going to. Everyone agrees with me. I'm just not smart enough.

options.A: Ask follow-up questions throughout the peer fellow session to model appropriate conversational skills for the student.
options.B: Use specific conceptual Biology questions with a limited range of possible answers rather than broad, open-ended questions during the session.
options.C: Establish the working practices of the peer fellow session through consensus via a study group pledge and, thereafter, consistently reinforce it.
options.D: Advise the student to take a 5-15 minute break after every hour of studying and a 30-minute break after two hours, always returning to the task punctually.
